title: A task closed: checkpoint before the next subject
text: You just closed a task. Before you start the next subject, write one NEXT line where your work keeps it (what is done, the ids, commits and paths, what comes next) and file anything durable with brain.py remember. Then the coming compaction loses nothing. It comes at about 300k tokens now, on Claude and on Codex.

title: A final report ends a subject
text: That report closed a subject. Its details no longer need to ride along in every turn. Check that the NEXT line and the checklist entry hold the ids, then take the next subject from a lean context, not one carrying the finished one.

title: Pushed or landed: write the ids down
text: Commit and landing ids survive a compaction only if they are written down. Put the ids you just produced into the NEXT line or the report now, while they are on screen.

title: A new ask on a full context: checkpoint first
text: This session holds about {k}k tokens and a new ask just arrived. If it is a new subject, spend one step writing the NEXT line for the old one. Compaction will then clear the old subject without losing it, and every turn after gets cheaper.

title: A headless worker that finished its stage should exit
text: A headless worker that has finished its stage should write its result to disk and exit. The runner starts the next stage in a fresh session from the NEXT line, which costs far less than resuming a long one.

title: Past 250k tokens: bring the subject to a stopping point
text: This session holds about {k}k tokens, and every turn re-reads all of it. Auto-compaction triggers near 300k. Bring the current subject to a stopping point and write the NEXT line, so the compaction falls on a clean boundary and not mid-thought.

title: Compaction is close: write down what the summary must keep
text: Compaction is a few turns away. Make sure your notes name the user's open asks with their task ids, the mesh claims you hold, the peer messages you owe an answer and the files you were editing. A summary keeps what is written down, not what is merely on screen.

title: This session predates the 300k setting
text: At about {k}k tokens this session started before the 300k auto-compact setting, and it will not compact by itself until it nears 1M. At the next subject boundary, write the NEXT line and say in one line that it is safe to /compact. Or finish, and let a fresh session take the next subject.

title: The cost of a turn is its whole context
text: A turn at {k}k tokens costs about {x} times a turn at 100k, and the finished work it carries is already saved. Compacting at the next boundary is the cheapest speed-up available.

title: Idle for a long time on a large context
text: This session sat idle about {m} minutes, so the prompt cache has expired and this turn re-reads {k}k tokens at full price. If the new ask is a new subject, write the NEXT line and work from a compacted or fresh context.

title: A large tool result now rides in every turn
text: That tool result was about {n}k characters, and it now rides in every later turn until the next compaction. Save what you need from it to a file or the NEXT line. Read the next one through a summary script, grep or head instead of whole.

title: Read big files by part
text: That read brought about {n}k characters into context. Read big files by offset and limit, or grep for the part you need. A whole-file read stays in every turn until the next compaction.

title: Cap command output at the source
text: That command printed about {n}k characters. Cap output where it is made (| tail -20, | cut -c1-200, a quiet flag) and send full logs to a file you read only if you need to. Every printed line is paid for again on each later turn.

title: Many small steps on a large context
text: {c} tool calls since the last prompt, at about {k}k tokens: each one re-reads the whole context. Fold the small steps into one script and take fewer, larger turns.

title: Keep a subagent's conclusion, not its transcript
text: Take the subagent's conclusion and the paths it names. Do not paste its transcript into the conversation or re-read its files in full; what it found is already on disk.

title: Save the lesson before the compaction, not after
text: If this subject taught something durable, file it now with brain.py remember, while the evidence is in front of you. After the compaction you will have the summary, not the evidence.

title: Just compacted: start from the NEXT line
text: This session was just compacted. Before acting, read your NEXT line, the checklist entries under your id and your mesh inbox. Trust what they record as done, and re-check only what could have changed since.

title: Compaction summaries are kept as brain nodes
text: Every compaction summary is saved as a node under ~/.claude/brain_graph/compactions/ (index: INDEX.jsonl), Codex's included. To see what an earlier compaction kept, or what this one dropped, read the node there rather than redoing the work.

title: Resume from the NEXT line
text: Pick up from the NEXT line and the checklist, not from what the old context seemed to say. They are the records a compaction cannot blur, and reading them costs less than re-deriving.

title: Codex compacts at 300k now
text: Codex now compacts by itself at 300k tokens (model_auto_compact_token_limit; it was 800k). At about {k}k, keep the NEXT line current at every subject end so the compaction is lossless, and its summary is saved as a brain node by the sweep.

title: Checkpoint on disk: the safe moment to compact
text: Your NEXT line is written. If the subject is done, close it in the checklist; from here a compaction loses nothing, so let it come (or say in one line that /compact is safe).

title: A released claim ends a task
text: You released a claim, so a task has ended. Put what it produced in the NEXT line; the next task should not carry this one's tool output.

title: A commit is a natural compaction point
text: A commit just recorded this step. Its id is the handle you will need later; write it in the NEXT line and treat everything the commit captured as safe to compact.

title: Tests passed: keep the result, drop the run
text: The test run passed. Keep one line (which suite, how many passed, at which commit) and let the run's output go; no summary needs it.

title: A handoff sent: the other agent holds it now
text: You handed work to another agent. Everything it needs is in the message; you need only its id and what you expect back. Write that in the NEXT line and drop the detail.

title: A report file written ends a subject
text: The report is on disk. Its contents need not stay in your context: keep its path in the NEXT line and start the next subject lean.

title: A gate decision recorded: the evidence can go
text: The decision is recorded with its evidence on disk. Keep the decision file's name and the lead's sha; the quotes and diffs you read can leave the context.

title: 200k tokens: plan where this subject ends
text: At about {k}k tokens, plan the boundary: finish the current step, then checkpoint. The automatic compaction near 300k should land on that boundary, not in the middle of a step.

title: Many files read: keep the findings, not the files
text: You have read {r} files since the last prompt. Write one line of what each one told you and let the reads go; re-reading later costs less than carrying them in every turn.

title: A long run of steps on one ask
text: {c} steps since the last prompt. If the ask is answered, stop and report; if not, write what is done before the next stretch, because a compaction can land in the middle of it.

title: The user switched subject: close the last one
text: The user has moved on to another subject. Close the previous one in one line (the NEXT line or the checklist entry), so the next compaction can drop it whole.

title: The user's correction goes on disk before anything else
text: Record the user's correction in your notes, and in the brain if it is durable, before acting on it. A compaction must never be the thing that erases what the user corrected.

title: Repeated failures: write down what was tried
text: {e} failures since the last prompt. Write what was tried and why it failed in the NEXT line; after a compaction you must not retry what already failed.

title: A background job: note its handle
text: Note the background job's id, its output file and what it should produce in the NEXT line. That is how you find it again after a compaction.

title: A page read: keep the quote and the address
text: Keep the lines you need with the address and the date you read them; the page itself should not ride in the context.

title: Intermediate results belong in files
text: Write intermediate results to a scratch file and read back only what the next step needs. A context is the most expensive place to keep data.

title: Past the 300k window: this session predates the setting
text: At about {k}k tokens this session is past the new 300k window, so it started before the setting. Finish the subject, write the checkpoint, and say that /compact is safe, or give the next subject to a fresh session.

title: One task per headless session
text: For a headless worker the cheapest compaction is a new session: one task per session, the next task seeded from the NEXT line, never a resumed session carrying the last task.

title: After a compaction: check your claims and inbox
text: A compaction does not release mesh claims, but what you remember of them is now a summary. Read your inbox and your claims before writing anything shared.

title: After a compaction: the user's newest words win
text: Read the user's newest prompts before you resume. A compacted summary can carry an older ask that the user has since changed.

title: End a subject with what is still open
text: End the subject by saying what is still open and who holds it. That line is what the summary and the next session start from.

title: Pushed and checked: the remote is the record
text: Once it is pushed and matched against the remote, the work is safe outside this session. Keep the commit id and drop the diff.

title: Mistakes go on record before a compaction
text: If something went wrong in this subject, add one line to MISTAKES.md now. A compacted summary rarely keeps the lesson, and the next session repeats what it does not know.

title: A summary keeps what is written, not the reasoning
text: A compaction keeps what is written in files, memories and the checklist, and loses the reasoning in between. Put your conclusions where they last before it comes.

title: Back after a gap: start from the records
text: After about {m} minutes away, start from the NEXT line, the checklist and the inbox. They are current; the context is old and costs full price to re-read now.

title: 'Continue' means the checkpoint, not the transcript
text: Continue from what the checkpoint says is next. Anything the checkpoint does not mention, check before trusting what the old context seemed to settle.

title: A helper's result: one line in, the rest on disk
text: Bring one line of the helper's result into your work and leave its full output in its file. A summary will keep the line and drop the transcript anyway.

title: Codex: one task per thread
text: A Codex thread that has finished its task should end. The next task is a new thread from the NEXT line, which costs far less than a long one carrying the last task.

title: Close the checklist and the NEXT line together
text: When you close a checklist entry, update the NEXT line in the same step. The two together are what lets any later compaction, or a fresh session, take up the work without loss.

title: Answer from the records, not the old context
text: On a full context, answer a new ask from the files and memories it concerns, not from what the old context seemed to say. The records are current; the context may have drifted.

title: Your compaction is a brain node now
text: Your compaction was saved as its own brain node, {node}. Its anchor in the memory folder links the compaction hub, this session's previous compaction, other sessions' compactions on your open tasks and the memories closest to it, so recall and the graph can reach it. Read it back with: python ~/.claude/dreaming/brain.py node {node} . If the summary dropped something you need, the full text is the file the anchor names.

title: Your compaction did not become a node
text: This session just compacted, but no brain node for it is in compactions/INDEX.jsonl yet. Rebuild it from the transcript: python -X utf8 ~/.claude/dreaming/compact_nodes.py --sweep --days 1 --claude-only . If it still does not appear, read compactions/errors.log and fix the cause; a compaction that is not a node is lost to the next session.

title: This Codex compaction has a linked record
text: Your context was compacted in this turn. Its linked record is {node}. If the native summary is opaque, that node holds boundary metadata only, so save a readable checkpoint: write a summary file (open asks, checklist ids, paths, claims, and a line starting NEXT:), run `python {tool} --summary <summary file> --session-id {sid} --rollout "{rollout}" --agent {agent}` to see the plan, then the same command with --save. Keep the NEXT line in STATUS.md current.
